articleTitle: The Enhancing Islamic Advertising Effectiveness Through Emotional Processes and Consumer-Centric Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research aimed to explore the perspectives of academicians on the role of emotions and feelings processes in enhancing the effectiveness of Islamic ads and identify elements that can increase the impact of Islamic advertising research in Malaysia. The study utilized semi-structured interviews to gather in-depth insights from the participants, aligning with the research objectives while adhering to Islamic principles. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, sixteen participants conducted virtual interviews using Webex software. The findings demonstrated the unique value of neuromarketing in providing valuable information beyond traditional methods in accordance with Islamic ethical guidelines. Moreover, the research identified elements such as color, music, symbols, and words that can enhance Islamic advertising effectiveness while maintaining Islamic values and principles. This knowledge can enable the inclusion of consumer-centric elements rooted in Islamic teachings, allowing advertisers to better meet the needs of Muslim consumers and design more compelling and attractive TV ads that align with Islamic values.

articleTitle: Business Crisis Management and Quintuple Helix Involvement of MSME: Post COVID-19 Empirical Study in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: As one of the pillars of the Indonesian economy, MSMEs are feeling the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic. All MSME sector movements must follow strict health protocols. The adoption of innovative technology and the synergy of various parties in the Quintuple Helix circle of actors play a role in encouraging Indonesian MSMEs to return to business. This study quantitatively examines the role of Covid-19 knowledge, technology, innovation, and Quintuple Helix actors in encouraging Indonesian MSMEs to survive during the Covid-19 pandemic. This study uses the PLS-SEM testing tool to measure the responses of 543 respondents from the Java Region. Quantitative Analysis Shows Positive Significance of P-Value 0.000 Between Covid-19 Common Knowledge on Technology Adoption, Quintuple Helix, and Innovative Performance. This means knowledge about Covid-19 makes MSME owners run technology systems and business operational innovations. However, this research also raises the perception that technology does not affect the survival ability of Indonesian MSMEs. This is because, in today's era, technology is mandatory for adoption. Meanwhile, innovation performance greatly affects the resilience of Indonesian MSME businesses during the Covid-19 pandemic. Quintuple Helix actors reinforce for MSMEs to survive through their respective roles. This research shows that good MSME resilience will improve the business performance of Indonesian MSMEs during the Covid-19 Pandemic.

articleTitle: Green Finance for Sustainable Development: A Bibliographic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive literature assessment investigating the contribution of green finance to the SDGs and the advancement of sustainable financial practices in businesses. This research examines a wide variety of academic articles, reports, and case studies to determine the effectiveness of green finance in advancing sustainability efforts and aligning financial investments with ESG standards. In this analysis, we highlight the ways in which green finance contributes to understanding the SDGs and promotes sustainable business practices. The research reveals that green finance plays a critical role in directing funds towards environmentally friendly endeavors, including renewable energy, energy efficiency, sustainable infrastructure, and climate change initiatives. Green finance actively supports the SDGs by providing financing for projects that contribute to environmental protection, social inclusion, and economic growth. Furthermore, based on the literature review, green finance encompasses investments in renewable energy development, environmentally friendly transportation projects, energy efficiency financing, environmental restoration, green infrastructure development, green bond issuance, investments in sustainable companies, and green microfinancing. All of these aim to support projects and investments that prioritize environmental sustainability and mitigate negative impacts on the environment.

articleTitle: Literature Review on Algorithmic Trading in Financial Markets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The financial market has drastically changed because of technological development. One of the most critical developments in this area is algorithmic trading, which refers to using computers to execute transactions. The role of algorithmic trading in financial markets has increased exponentially over the last decade; however, a literature review is scant. In this study, we aim to plug this research gap. We initially retrieved 2007 articles from the Scopus database using a defined search string. Keeping this research to the subject confined and selecting only articles from prestigious journals, 30 articles are selected for this review. This study highlights that the existing study highly emphasized the effect of algorithmic trading on liquidity, volatility, investors' emotions, and the discovery of stock prices. Furthermore, some future guidelines are also suggested through this review.

articleTitle: Digital Gold in Emerging Markets: An Investor's Perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The digital revolution in the gold market has led to the emergence of digital gold as a form of investment. Digital When compared to the physical manner of investment, gold has a much greater potential to generate returns than any other asset type. It does, however, also have certain possible hazards, such as the possibility of fraud, market risk, expenditures, etc. The goal of the current study was to determine how well-informed retail investors were about digital gold. Additionally, it wants to research how investors view this new investment possibility. The findings indicate that a lack of understanding of the idea among investors prevents them from making Digital Gold investments. People who invest in digital gold say they do it because it is convenient and requires no storage.

articleTitle: Political Stability and Nonperforming Loans: Evidence from Jordanian Banks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The reasons for defaulting on loans and the factors associated with defaulting on loans have been discussed in many previous studies. Despite the abundance of research dealing with non-performing loans and their causes, there are very few studies linking non-performing loans to political stability. The research concentrated on explaining the reasons for defaulting on loans in Jordan between 1998 and 2018. Three estimators DFE, PMG, and MG were used in the model. It was found that low rates of return on assets, return on equity, political stability, and GDP growth all raise non-performing loan rates in the long run. High inflation rates and interest rate spreads raise the rates of non-performing loans.

articleTitle: Analysis Impact of the Production Technology Used by MSMEs on Consumer Satisfaction and Loyalty
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Advances in technology are believed to be able to increase sales, because technology is considered capable of making work more effective so that costs incurred become efficient. However, the use of technology has not been widely used by SMEs. Especially during the Covid-19 pandemic, the economy underwent quite significant changes, starting from a decrease in turnover to consumer behavior that made everything online. The purpose of this research is to prove whether the use of production technology has an impact on consumer satisfaction and consumer loyalty. This research uses primary data from 110 consumers who have filled out a questionnaire, these consumers have ordered online. The research results show that, Partially, production technology, packaging safety, employee skills, price and consumer satisfaction have a positive influence on customer satisfaction. variables production technology, packaging safety, employee skills and price determine the consumer satisfaction variable by 65%. Partially, production technology, price and consumer satisfaction have a positive influence on customer loyalty. variables production technology, price and consumer sarisfaction determine the consumer loyalty variable by 72.3%.

articleTitle: ICT Impact on Jordan's Economic Growth from 2000 to 2019
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: In recent years, there has been increased discussion about the importance of information and communications technology (ICT), particularly in terms of how it facilitates the work of individuals and businesses. For example, Jordan's ICT sector has enabled the country to diversify its economy and makes it one of the most advanced in the Middle East. This study employs multiple regression analysis to examine the impact of ICT on Jordan's economic growth from 2000–2019. There are several economic theories that have examined the relationship between ICT and economic growth. These theories offer different perspectives on this topic. Theories on economic growth suggest that ICT can either increase labor productivity and efficiency (neoclassical growth theory) or lead to economic growth by generating new ideas and innovations (endogenous growth theory). From these two theories, ICT obviously contributes to economic growth. The empirical analysis shows that imports of ICT goods, the number of mobile subscriptions, and the use of the Internet by individuals have a positive and significant impact on the economic growth of Jordan's gross domestic product (GDP). These ICT indicators have contributed to this growth by improving the productivity and efficiency of the Jordanian economy and facilitating trade and investment. Nevertheless, ICT goods exports had a negative impact on Jordan's GDP, which could make sense given that the ICT industry in Jordan is still in a growth phase.

articleTitle: The Impact of Ownership Structure on Accounting Conservatism in GCC Countries
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to examine the impact of ownership structure on accounting conservatism among the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries' publicly listed firms. By using the multivariant regression model, the results of this study show a significant association between the firms' ownership structure variables (i e. foreign ownership and largest shareholder ownership) and accounting conservatism. This study provides new evidence on the importance of ownership structure variables and their impact on the firm's accounting conservatism in emerging stock markets. The results of this study are undoubtedly of great interest to the regulatory bodies, shareholders, and governments in the GCC countries. Also, the results of this study can be used as a guideline by the stakeholders to set a sound and efficient ownership structure that can support the organization in minimizing the agency problem. The study findings can provide a valuable insight to the shareholders in GCC countries and aid in understating the impact of different ownership structures on accounting conservatism.

articleTitle: Prospect of Blue Economy in Gulf Cooperation Council States: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The blue economy (BE) is a vital opportunity for the GCC countries to achieve sustainable development by harnessing the potential of their marine resources. This paper argues that regional cooperation is essential to address the challenges and opportunities of the BE sectors, such as pollution, climate change, resource management, and biodiversity conservation. This paper explores the opportunities and challenges of developing a BE in the GCC countries and examines how these countries can leverage their marine resources to generate economic benefits while protecting the environment and ensuring sustainability. It also discusses the future prospects and directions of the BE in the GCC region, and proposes a unified framework for assessing the impacts of the BE activities and suggests ways to enhance regional and global partnerships, technical capacity, and social inclusion.

articleTitle: The Bahraini Real Estate Market and the Changing Business Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Given the current rapidly evolving world, real estate and property management firms are expected to deliver exceptional customer experience and meet the stakeholders' needs in the sector. In the Kingdom of Bahrain, despite the government's national recovery plan to address the impact of COVID-19, there is a dearth of information regarding key stakeholders' perspectives on the challenges in real estate and property management. This research was conducted to assess the challenges faced by property management companies in the changing business environment and their response to the rising standards and expectations of tenants and property owners in Manama, Kingdom of Bahrain.

articleTitle: The Effectiveness of Islamic Microfinance for Solving the Problems of Unemployment, Poverty, and Poor Standard of Living
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The objective of this study is to examine the effectiveness of Islamic microfinance in solving the problems of unemployment, poverty., and poor standard of living in Muslim countries. The study aims at assessing the impact of Islamic microfinance on women's employment and evaluating its contribution to social and economic empowerment as well as providing recommendations for addressing the overall challenges for unemployment., poverty., and poor standard of living. The methodology involves a systematic review of the literature as well as analysing current studies., reports., and case studies related to Islamic microfinance and employment for women. Quantitative data analysis will be employed to measure the employment outcomes of women participation in Islamic microfinance programs. The findings show that., in addition to facilitating access to funding and the provision of financial products., Islamic microfinance positively impacts on creating employment opportunities for women. The creation of self-employment opportunities and the enhancement of women's economic wellbeing are contributing to social and economic entrepreneurship. The research suggests that the Islamic Microfinance provides funds and supports and thus positively contributes by strengthening collaboration., promoting financial literacy., and entrepreneurship training as well as provides improved market access. This study reveals the uniqueness of Islamic microfinance's positive impact on women's employment and inclusive development in Muslim countries.

articleTitle: Do Financial Literacy and Digital Technology Drive Investment Intention Among Gen Z in the Islamic Capital Market: A Mediating Role of Risk Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study intends to empirically explore and analyse the effects of financial literacy and digital technology on investing intention in the Islamic capital market among Generation Z (Gen Z) in Banda Aceh City, Indonesia. It also attempts to assess how risk tolerance affects investment intentions in a mediating way. Out of 37,892 Gen Z in the city, 125 of them made up the study's sample, selected using the purposive sampling technique. The study collected the primary data by sending questionnaires to the selected respondents and assessed using the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) approach. The study recorded that the Gen Z interest in investing in the Islamic capital market and risk tolerance were positively impacted by financial literacy and digital technology. The study also discovered that the impact of financial literacy and digital technology on investing intentions is mediated by risk tolerance. These findings highlight the crucial role of enhancing financial literacy and advancing digital technology in boosting Gen Z's risk tolerance and stimulate their interest in investing monies in the Islamic capital market.

articleTitle: Entrepreneurship Development and Sustainability in Islamic Nations: Case of Jordan
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The purpose of the paper is to explore the status of entrepreneurship education at all Jordanian universities. The study employed descriptive analytics using a survey and a web search of all Jordanian universities. The key findings of this study are that even though Jordanian universities provide a variety of entrepreneurship courses; entrepreneurship education is not yet effectively integrated into the curricula of all Jordanian higher education institutions. The findings also showed that entrepreneurship education generally relies on theoretical knowledge and is taught from a business administration perspective. The study recommends that; entrepreneurship courses should be properly incorporated into the curricula of all disciplines of study. Higher education policymakers should seek to ensure a realistic model for teaching entrepreneurship.

articleTitle: Islamic Banking Services and their Effects on Bahrain's Economy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Islamic banking services have become increasingly popular in Bahrain, as they operate based on Shariah principles that emphasize interest free, ethical, and socially responsible business practices. This study examines the effects of Islamic banking services on Bahrain's economy. The paper finds that Islamic banking services have had a positive impact on Bahrain's economy, as they have promoted financial inclusion, entrepreneurship, and small business development. Islamic banks offer financing solutions that are based on profit and loss sharing (PLS) which can provide more accessible and flexible funding options for small businesses and start-ups. This, in turn, can lead to the creation of new jobs and opportunities for people in the community. In addition, Islamic banking services have contributed to the development of the Islamic capital market in Bahrain, which has attracted investment from both domestic and international investors. This has helped to diversify Bahrain's economy and reduce its dependence on oil revenues. The paper also notes that Islamic banking services have contributed to the growth of the real estate sector in Bahrain, as Islamic banks offer financing solutions that are compliant with Shariah principles. This has led to an increase in demand for Shariah-compliant real estate financing, which has supported the growth of the real estate sector in Bahrain. The findings of this study suggests that Islamic banking services have had a positive impact on Bahrain's economy, promoting financial inclusion, entrepreneurship, and small business development, contributing to the development of the Islamic capital market, and supporting the growth of the real estate sector.

articleTitle: Evaluating Natural Resources, Renewable Energy, Financial Development, and Ecological Footprint in G20 Countries
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Financial instruments' development is the key factor that can be used to resolve the rising challenges of climate change and lookforward to a sustainable economy. To assess this issue in the G20 countries, the relationship between natural resources (NR), renewable energy (RE), financial development (FD), economic growth (EG), and ecological footprint during the period 1990–2018 was examined using the PMG-ARDL approach. The results show that NR and GDP have a positive and significant relationship with the ecological footprint in the short and long term. Although the FD and RE have indicated a negative and significant relationship with the environmental footprint. The relationship of human capital with the ecological footprint is significant in the short term. It is suggested that G20 countries should increase financial support to achieve sustainable development. It is also important to develop the technological aspect to reduce greenhouse emissions and household consumption of conventional energy.

articleTitle: Testing the Impact of Covid-19 on Weak form Efficiency Hypothesis for Sharia-Compliant Indices and Stocks: Evidence from Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Global shocks have a significant impact on stock markets, which is reflected on stock prices movements, trading volume and investors' willingness to invest. In addition, they could result in making stocks highly correlated and could cause serial correlations for a given stock. This could convert a stock market to be weak form inefficient that has huge impact on investors, listed companies and policy makers. This study aims to investigate the impact of the COVID-19 global outbreak on the Bahrain Islamic Index and its components weak form efficiency. To achieve its main objective, the study tests whether the daily returns of the index and its components are serially independent and identically distributed (following Random Walk Hypothesis RWH). The daily returns are calculated for the period between April 2015 and April 2023. Each company's and index's dataset are divided into 2 subsets (pre and during COVID-19) and, variance ratio, Runs and Phillips-Perron (PP) tests are implemented to test the Random Walk Hypothesis. The empirical findings suggest that the index and 50% of its components were weak-form inefficient during the pandemic. The study also presented a number of recommendations to both investors and stock market policymakers to help mitigate the negative impact of market inefficiency during abnormal periods.

articleTitle: How Do Prices React to the Dividend Announcement? Conventional vs Islamic Stock Markets in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research is an event study, aiming at observing the stock markets' reaction to dividend announcements using the abnormal return indicator. This study covers a four-year period, from 2019 to 2022. The event window is set as three-day before and three-day after the dividend announcement. A number of 50 companies were selected as the sample of the study consists of each 25 Islamic stocks and 25 conventional stocks. The research employs a documentation method, primarily sourcing data from the official website of the Indonesia Stock Exchange, by collecting daily closing stock prices during the observation period. The study's findings revealed the presence of abnormal return differences both before and after the dividend announcement, for both Shariah-compliant and conventional company stocks. The findings further signify that the different stock market reactions as indicated by the differences in the abnormal returns to the dividend announcements.

articleTitle: Accountability of Islamic Boarding School: A Comparative Insights from Modern and Traditional Pesantren in Aceh, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Being part of the Islamic economic ecosystem, pesantren has been recognized as a sustainable Islamic educational institution in Indonesia which not only sustain its own financing yet some even create economic benefits to their surrounding communities. Nevertheless, ambiguity arises with regard to the accounting and accountability practice of these institutions considering lack of regulation and enforcement of financial accountability for these institutions. Therefore, this study aims to explore the accountability practice of pesantren taking the context of the different types and nature of modern and traditional pesantren in Aceh, Indonesia. Aceh is by far the only province in Indonesia which attempts to implement sharia principles in all aspects including financial realm. Qualitative approach was utilized involving in-depth interviews with pertinent individuals at both types of pesantren in Aceh. It was revealed that modern and traditional pesantren in Aceh have realized good accountability. However, modern pesantren still needs to pay attention in publishing its financial reports, while traditional pesantren needs to significantly improve the quality of its financial reports. This study implies that accounting and accountability have been imbued within the practice of pesantren either modern or traditional yet the extent, nature and quality of the practice which still vary and necessitate for further improvements.

articleTitle: Customers' preference for Islamic banks over conventional banks in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Islamic banking has become a popular alternative to conventional banking in many parts of the world, including Bahrain. This study examines whether the customers prefer Islamic banking over conventional banking in Bahrain or not. The results show that customers value Islamic banking products and services that avoid interest-based transactions, such as sharia-compliant financing and investment options. The study finds that many customers are willing to switch to Islamic banks in the future, citing factors such as ethical considerations and a desire to avoid interest-based transactions. The study concludes an in-depth analysis of the findings as well as its limitations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Efficiency at Abu Dhabi Primary School
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficiency of primary schools located in the United Arab Emirates, with a special focus on the Abu Dhabi educational zone. This study was conducted with Grade 4 students in the school selected for the study. School efficiency was evaluated using discretionary variables as inputs and students' academic achievement as outputs. The results of the Data Envelopment Analysis revealed that only four schools had a medium level of efficiency, whereas the majority of schools had a high level of technical efficiency (over 0.81). The empirical findings of this study were utilized to develop better public policies by identifying best practices and areas for potential improvement.

articleTitle: Economic Growth — Climate Change Nexus in GCC States: A Panel ARDL Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The current study examines the relationship between economic growth and climate change in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nations, with a particular emphasis on the effect of economic growth on regional carbon emissions. A Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model is employed in the study to examine the short-run and long-run relationships between economic growth and climate change variables. According to the study's findings, there is a statistically significant relationship between the GDP growth dimension and several variables, such as carbon emissions, yearly average temperature, annual average precipitation, population density, and annual crude oil production. The study concludes that there is a need for GCC authorities to consider the environmental consequences of economic expansion and take actions to prevent the negative effects of climate change. The paper underlines the necessity of international cooperation in addressing climate change and promoting renewable energy in the GCC countries.

articleTitle: Investigating the Relationship Between Inflation and Financial Development: Evidence from Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the relationship between inflation and financial development in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. By using yearly data gathered on inflation, GDP growth and domestic credit as a percentage of GDP from 2002 to 2022, this study has used the regression analysis to examine whether the relationship between the variables is positive or negative. The findings suggest that there is a negative relationship between inflation, GDP growth and domestic credit. It can be concluded that higher levels of inflation have a greater negative impact on the financial development of a country.

articleTitle: The Expansionary Effects of Sukuk in Economic Growth
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Among the Islamic financial products, Sukuk are the most dynamic interest free modes of financing, and such instruments offer creative approach to raise money while being in line with Shariah standards. Sukuk are issued against assets and therefore, these are asset-backed securities, and they can be traded, and provide investors with Ijara and similar income which are less volatile in nature. Sukuk can be used to fund projects for economic growth, infrastructural improvements, and the creation of new goods and services. It can also be used as a source of funding business endeavours like mergers and acquisitions, the expansion of manufacturing facilities, and the creation of new goods and services. Sukuk can also be utilized to finance the construction of roads, bridges, and other forms of infrastructure. Sukuk are Islamic financial instruments that can be used to finance the development of new products, real estate ventures, business growth, infrastructural improvements, and the creation of new products. It provides investors with the funding they need, and they get a share of the sales proceeds when the real estate units are sold or rented. Sukuk can offer investors a safer and more reliable return on their investment than conventional bonds, and it is compliant with Shariah guidelines. For example, a business might issue Sukuk to pay for the creation of a brand-new product such as multi storied office building, and investors would receive a portion of the earnings when the real estate is sold or rented.

articleTitle: FDI Inflow in Emerging Economies: An Empirical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The movement of FDI inflow is changing, and the entire globe is watching it. The inflow of foreign direct investment into the global economy is declining for developed nations while rising for emerging ones. Due to their favorable demographic, geographic, and economic characteristics, emerging economies are ideal for international investment. Current happenings worldwide, such as the Epidemic and the Sino-American trade dispute, have provided a wealth of chances for emerging economies. Though the anticipated proportion of inward flow of foreign investment by the most appropriate ARIMA model indicated an increasing movement and followed the historical direction concluded the course of the existing period, the historical trend of internal movement of FDI showed a growing tendency regarding emerging markets in the previous existences. The learning's conclusions will assist overseas stakeholders in defining the direction of FDI inflow into emerging economies and making investment decisions.

articleTitle: Financial Distress, Survival and Performance of Saudi Arabian Companies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Financial distress refers to the position where a firm's cash flows are not sufficient to meet the required payment. In any organization the adverse effect of financial distress can threaten the survival of the firm. Literature shows that various factors are included in the financial distress determinant including firm size, liquidity, profitability, solvency, efficiency and market. In this study, we employ 42 ratios from four group of ratios. The descriptive statistics showed that no outliers are present. The correlation matrix is calculated to find the correlation among the ratios and Bartlett test and KMO tests validate our data. 18 ratios are finalized based on our direct correlation matrix analysis and factor analysis is done on these ratios. Explanatory Factor analysis is performed, and three factors are determined. Our results showed that are most important set of ratios in determining the financial distress of Saudi companies include leverage, liquidity and efficiency set of ratios. Our results showed the eight most important ratios that are predictive of the financial distress.

articleTitle: Examining the Determinants of Non-Performing Loans and Bank Performance in E7 Countries
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study examines the determinants of non-performing loans in the E7 states namely Brazil, China, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Russia, and Turkiye by using annual panel data spanning from the years 2000 to 2020. The fully modified ordinary least squares (FMOLS) regression and dynamic ordinary least squares (DOLS) were used. The findings show that return on assets, loan-to-deposits ratio (LDR), capital adequacy ratio (CAR), real effective exchange rate, unemployment rate, and inflation rate have a significant impact on nonperforming loans (NPLs). The gross domestic product growth rate was found to be statistically insignificant. Thus, it is advised for banks of E7 states to implement more advanced credit-worthiness assessments. In addition, they should pay close attention to capital adequacy, focusing on growing regulatory capital.

articleTitle: Modeling the Relative Efficiency of Islamic Banks in Bahrain Using Data Envelopment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research evaluated the performance of Bahrain's Islamic retail banks from 2017 to 2019. The study uses data envelopment analysis (DEA) models to assess the relative efficiency of banks. Six Islamic banks are included in the sample. Total deposits, fixed assets, and owner's equity were picked as inputs, and facility credits, total operational revenue, and net profit were chosen as outputs. The study identified input and output inefficiencies in banks that weren't doing well and proposed input and output targets that would aid banks in improving their performance. The key advantage is that this research should add to existing studies on the effectiveness of Islamic banks by providing banks, regulators, investors, and researchers with additional information. Policymakers could benefit from knowing how specific factors affect efficiency since it could help them advocate, disapprove, or change a policy.

articleTitle: Modelling Islamic Business and Online Communication Ethics: A Literature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Islamic business ethics is the study of the application of Islamic principles and values in business. As businesses have become more globalised in recent years, the discipline has expanded significantly in its infancy. Ethics in Internet communication is a subfield that looks at the ethical implications of utilising the internet for interaction. The discipline is also relatively new, but it has expanded significantly in recent years as internet access has become ubiquitous. The purpose of this study is to investigate how Islamic ethical principles and practises affect business and communication interactions online. The research looks at how Islamic values and beliefs influence business ethics and online interactions. This study aims to add to the current literature on business ethics and give insights for individuals and organisations working in culturally diverse environments by gaining awareness of the distinctive ethical viewpoints of Islam.

articleTitle: Challenges of Islamic Finance in Increasing the Market Share and the Possible Solutions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Islamic finance has made significant progress in home and abroad and in all sectors of the economy, including in legal and ethical aspects of life. This study seeks to define the legal framework for Islamic banking and to explain the role of challenges to it so that systems can be compared, and the experiences of the Islamic banks can be evaluated. This paper emphasizes the distinction between Islamic finance arrangements and other financing options in a global legal context. The growth of Islamic finance is being influenced by numerous factors, including the growing Muslim population, the surge in interest in ethical investing, and the need for financial services that adhere to Shariah. Islamic finance and Islamic economics are challenged by several problems, including lack of knowledge, supply constraints, higher prices, complexities, lack of liquidity, regulatory uncertainty, lack of political commitment, social and cultural barriers, and ignorance. This study attempts to explore all such challenges and offer a modest roadmap for overcoming such challenges.

articleTitle: Women Entrepreneurs: New Research Horizons-Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Countries across the globe are working diligently to make the ecosystem conducive for the development of entrepreneurial streak. The governments are working closely to promote women's entrepreneurship. The Indian government has also taken multiple initiatives to ensure that women take up entrepreneurship. With these initiatives, women are adding to the nation's economic growth and contributing to their personal wealth. An in-depth literature of Scopus-indexed journals reveals that research on women entrepreneurs is on the rise. Through this study, the author unravels a whole new area of research for women entrepreneurs which is personal investments. The existing literature is on comparative of men and women investors. It is a well-established fact that men and women think differently. An in-depth inquiry on what are the biases that influence personal investment decision-making in this growing segment will help the financial service providing organizations to train their staff and develop products which cater to this new segment. The other areas of research that can be done in detail include what are the biases that women face when they get a seat on the table and when they take their ventures for funding to venture capitalists.

articleTitle: Forecasting Crude Oil Price Using SARIMAX Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Oil prices have a significant impact on a nation's economy, and forecasting its prices is essential for effective economic planning and decision-making. However, numerous factors contribute to the volatility of oil prices, making the task of predicting it difficult. This research aims to forecast the oil price and to know the effect of changing the oil price on the global economy. To reach the best results, the secondary data methodology was used, where the closing price of crude oil was collected through the investing.com website for the period from January 2008 to June 2023, and the SARIMAX machine learning model was used to obtain the prediction. The results demonstrated that the price of crude oil will decline in the coming year, and the possible reasons for that are geopolitical tensions due to the Russian-Ukrainian war, the world's tendency to use alternative energy, the political situation between countries and the OPEC control over the oil price. It is advised that investors be cautious and invest in oil prices with specific risks in mind.

articleTitle: Resilience of Islamic Banks in Bahrain: A Comparative Study of the 2007 Global Financial Crisis and the Covid-19 Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This paper examines the differential impacts of the 2007 credit crisis and the Covid-19 pandemic on Islamic banks, focusing on their performance and stability. Utilizing accounting data from three leading Islamic banks in Bahrain and employing fixed effects panel models, we investigate the consequences of these financial shocks. The study reveals that the Covid-19 pandemic has a more significant indirect impact on Islamic banks' performance compared to the 2007 credit crunch. We attribute this finding to the reliance of Islamic banks on Profit-Loss Sharing and investment activities now constrained by uncer-tainty and tight economic conditions. The findings contribute to the literature on Islamic banking and finance, emphasizing the importance of ethical principles and risk-sharing mechanisms in navigating financial turmoil. The study's implications are relevant for policymakers, regulators, and practitioners seeking to understand the resilience and advantages of Islamic banking systems in turbulent economic environments.

articleTitle: Forecasting Twitter's Favorite Cryptocurrencies Based on a Comparative Assessment of SARIMA, LSTM and Fb Prophet Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The complicated combination of long-term patterns, short-term seasonality, and uncertainty has made selecting an appropriate forecasting model for cryptocurrency prices challenging. To forecast the future prices of the cryptocurrencies, this study compared three machine learning models: the Seasonal Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and the Facebook (Fb) Prophet for the period of 2017 till 2023. It was discovered that the FbProphet model works well in predicting the daily price forecasts of Bitcoin and Dogecoin with low mean squared error (MSE), using time series datasets from 2017 through 2023 as the training data to anticipate 12 months of unseen data. While predicting the future from 2023 to 2024, Fb Prophet stated that Dogecoin is most likely to remain stable while Bitcoin price is most likely to continue falling. The LSTM model performs better than the other models based on forecasting results.

articleTitle: Assess the role of the OPEC Fund in Achieving Sustainable Financial Development in Islamic Nations: Descriptive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The study aims at assessing the effect of the OPEC Fund on sustainable financial development in Islamic countries during the period 2017–2022. The study adopts a descriptive approach to present the theoretical background and literature review of the role of development financial institutions in achieving sustainable development, as well as review the role of the OPEC Fund in global development finance and illustrate its main funded projects in strategic sectors of Islamic countries. The study's key findings are that the OPEC Fund collaborates with governments and the business sector, as well as other financial organizations, to provide loans, grants, and technical assistance to different strategic sectors. These findings are consistent with economic theories and earlier research. Therefore, the study proposes recommendations to expand OPEC's financial support for Islamic states in order to boost economic growth and accomplish sustainable development goals by 2030.

articleTitle: Impact of Oil Price Shocks on GCC Stock Markets: New Evidence from NARDL Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The aim of this document is to measure the asymmetric and nonlinear effects of oil price shocks on stock markets in GCC region during the Ukrainian crisis. For this purpose, research in this paper utilizes the nonlinear Autoregressive Distributed Lag (NARDL) and data on GCC stock price indices and oil price from January 2020 until July 2023. The main outcomes of this study demonstrate that both positive and negative shocks in oil prices have significant effect on stock markets performance in GCC region in short and long-term periods. Moreover, these effects tend to have nonlinear trajectories over long-term periods except for stock indices in Saudi Arabia and UAE. The results of this study affirm that policy markets and regulatory authorities in GCC region need to take further steps toward diversifying their economies with less dependence on oil exports and strengthening the financial system structure.

articleTitle: The Effects of Service Quality and Sharia Governance on Islamic Banking Customer Loyalty: Does Bank Reputation Play a Role?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to measure and analyze the moderating role of bank reputation on the effects of service quality and sharia governance on loyalty of the customers of Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) in Banda Aceh City, Indonesia. Of the 39,872 BSI customers, 125 of them were selected as the sample of the study using a purposive sampling technique. Primary data collection was carried out by distributing questionnaires to respondents and analyzed using the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) technique. The results of the study revealed that sharia governance and service quality have a significant positive effect on customer loyalty. The bank reputation has a significant moderated role in enhancing the effects on sharia governance and service quality on customer loyalty. These empirical results showed the importance of improving the quality of service and sharia governance in increasing customer loyalty would be enhanced by continuous improvements of bank reputation.

Author Keywords: customer loyalty of Bank Syariah Indonesia

articleTitle: A Nexus Between Green Human Resource Management, Environmental Values, and Green Service Behavior: The Moderating Role of Environmental Commitment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study draws an association between green HRM, environment values, and green service behavior with the moderating role of environment commitment based on the available literature. The qualitative and inductive research method was employed to study the potential association among the study variables by exploring existing literature. The literature indicates the potential association between GRS, GTD, environmental values, and green service behavior amongst employees of various industries. Moreover, the literature also sheds light on the crucial role of environmental commitment between GRS, GTD, and green service behavior. The literature also sheds light on an important aspect that environmental commitment amongst employees is inevitable to increase employees' green values through GRS and GTD.

articleTitle: Does Intellectual Capital Efficiency Matter for Firms' Investment Efficiency?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The determination of investment expenditures' compatibility with growth opportunities always remains a challenge for organizations. However, the efficient utilization of resources of firms may help them to overcome the challenge of over and under-investment. The present study examines the direct and indirect effect of intellectual capital efficiency (ICE) on firms' investment efficiency (IE) where the channel of indirect effect is the financial constraint (FC) faced by firms. For this, we developed a panel of 174 firms belonging to Pakistan from 2016 to 2020. In the first stage, we measure investment efficiency as a trichotomous variable under the categories of firms with over-investment, under-investment, and optimal (efficient) investment. In the second stage, we converted our panel data into cross-sectional data by taking an average of all variables and then used the multinomial logistic regression model to estimate the direct and indirect effect of intellectual capital efficiency on firms' investment efficiency. The findings of the present research reveal that although intellectual capital efficiency, measured by the E-VAIC model, does not have a direct effect on investment efficiency, it affects investment efficiency indirectly through the channel of financial constraint measured by Z-Score. Therefore, firms should work on the enhancement of the efficiency of their intellectual capital to avoid the problem of inefficient investment.

articleTitle: Unleashing the Challenges During the Pandemic - Case Study of Two Indian Women Entrepreneurs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The sector of entrepreneurship that is expanding the fastest globally is that of female entrepreneurs. As a result of the increase in female entrepreneurs, India has seen enormous commercial and economic progress. Women-owned companies are significantly contributing to society by generating jobs across the country, affecting demographic shifts, and inspiring the next generation of female entrepreneurs. This paper talks about the two companies started and owned by female entrepreneurs during the Covid period and how the company is growing, strategies adopted and the challenges faced by both the women entrepreneurs. PG Digital Solution started by a young entrepreneur while studying graduation faced many challenges but the lessons learned from her entrepreneurial skills is an inspiration for the young generation. Nhea was the result of the collaboration of two ladies created with a common objective of women's issues supporting women microentrepreneurs and giving opportunities to participate in the supply chain.

articleTitle: Mapping Small Business Entrepreneurship Using Bibliometrics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Small Business Enterprises (SBEs) are sometimes viewed as smaller versions of large corporations, despite the fact that they differ from the latter in a number of ways. There are academic publications that discuss and put out numerous hypotheses about how socially conscious firms might create social value, but there aren't many empirical studies that actually apply tested effect-measuring methods to real-world company ventures. In this study, a bibliometric analytic approach is used to analyze and retrospectively analyze the continually expanding body of literature on SBEs. A co-word analysis of 119 texts found main themes regarding the different topics in each one. The findings show that early publications are typically descriptive, premature, and theoretical, i.e., the majority of studies advocate for and re-imagine a more sustainable, responsible, and equitable post-pandemic business, but very little research thoroughly examines whether, why, and how such theoretical proclamations are materializing or not, and/or whether they will remain a fuss caused by small business entrepreneurship. The report's conclusion on small business entrepreneurship makes a number of recommendations and areas for further study.

articleTitle: Transitioning Towards a Circular Economy: Role and Challenges of Corporates in India
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study explores the evolving landscape of India's transition towards a circular economy, focusing on the significant contribution of prominent corporations. In recent decades, the discernible ecological consequences of corporate activities have catalysed a fundamental change in approach towards sustainable methodologies following governmental aims to attain a state of zero-net emissions. At the core of this paradigm shift lies the notion of the circular economy. This approach prioritises minimising waste and optimising resource efficiency, all within the framework of the fundamental principles of ‘Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle.’ Adopting this paradigm can enhance India's resource efficiency, hence promoting long-term sustainability through reevaluating waste materials as valuable resources. This study aims to fully comprehend the shift towards a circular economy, elucidating the activities undertaken by many industries in India and its business executives. Studying the transition towards a circular economy in India is crucial as it addresses the urgent need for sustainable economic practices, helping mitigate environmental degradation and resource scarcity while aligning with global climate goals. Moreover, understanding the role of leading corporations in this transition is essential for shaping effective policies and strategies to drive India's sustainable development agenda.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Green Financing Initiatives Implemented by Banking Organizations in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study investigates the adoption of green banking and finance practices in the Kingdom of Bahrain's banking sector with the help of a case study approach. Analyzing annual reports and publications, the research evaluates ESG initiatives of three banks: HSBC Bahrain, Standard Chartered Bank (SCB) Bahrain, and the National Bank of Bahrain (NBB), and assesses the effectiveness and alignment of these practices with global sustainability goals. The literature review highlights the growing importance of integrating environmental, social, and governance considerations in banking operations. Existing research demonstrates the role of banks in promoting sustainability and aligning strategies with environmental and societal goals. With the help of a secondary research approach, the study synthesizes data from diverse sources. Results reveal distinct green initiatives of each bank. HSBC Bahrain focuses on net-zero emissions, social inclusion, and sustainable finance. SCB Bahrain emphasizes sustainable financial products, technology for ESG risk management, and stakeholder engagement. NBB Bahrain's approach includes board oversight, a sustainability committee, workforce awareness, and alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goals. The conclusions of this study point towards the commitment of these banks to sustainability. Recommendations include further collaboration, enhanced reporting, innovation, community engagement, and continuous improvement in ESG strategies. While limitations exist, including data reliance and potential gaps, the research provides valuable insights into Bahrain's green banking landscape, informing future sustainable finance endeavors.

articleTitle: Is Gold a Safe Heaven? Evidence from Time Series Forecasting Using Sarimax Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to utilize the SARIMAX model for forecasting the price of gold over the next 12 months. To accomplish this, the model was trained using gold close prices from 2013 to 2023. The results suggest that gold is a reliable safe-haven asset, and according to the SARIMAX model, the price of gold is expected to rise in the upcoming 12 months. The analysis was based on gold close price data from July 31, 2013, to July 31, 2023. The prediction results were presented in a graph, along with evaluation metrics. These findings highlight the accuracy and reliability of the SARIMAX model's predictions, which can be valuable for investors and researchers in their decision-making process. Therefore, based on these research findings, investing in gold is a favorable option, and the SARIMAX model stands as an effective forecasting tool.

articleTitle: Ethical Foundations and Fraud Prevention: A Study on the Role of Morality and Integrity in Indonesia's Islamic Banking Sector
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study examines the morality and integrity of employees in the Islamic banking industry on fraud prevention. The analytical method used in this study is PLS-SEM (Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modeling). The key insight gleaned from this study is the significant impact of strong ethical foundations, rooted in principles of morality and integrity, in mitigating the occurrence of fraud within the Islamic banking industry. Consequently, the findings of this research hold substantial implications, serving as a valuable set of recommendations aimed at assisting Islamic Commercial Banks operating in Indonesia to fortify their anti-fraud measures. By recognizing and fostering ethical conduct among their employees, these banks can establish a more resilient defense against fraudulent activities, ultimately safeguarding their operations and preserving the trust of their customers and stakeholders.

articleTitle: Technology Companies in Indonesia: How is the Financial Performance?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: It is believed that human progress of the times and technological advancements will be of assistance to technology firms in reaching optimal financial performance and prospering in their respective fields. The purpose of this study is to determine the relationship between the size of a company, its leverage, its growing sales, and its liquidity and its financial success, which will be assessed by its return on assets, return on equity, and return on investment. It is difficult to generalize about the impact that the independent variables have on the monetary output of businesses operating in the technology sector in Indonesia. The size of a corporation has a negative impact on a company's ROE and ROI, while having no effect on ROA. There is a wide range of consequences that can be caused by leverage, some of which include a positive influence on ROA, a negative impact on ROE, and no impact on ROI. The increase in sales has no impact whatsoever on ROA, ROE, or ROI. There is no effect of liquidity on ROE, but it does have a negative influence on ROA and ROI.

articleTitle: Key Resources for Circular Micro-Small Culinary Industry 4.0 Transformation: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Indonesian Culinary MSMEs support the Indonesian economy. With the development of Industry 4.0, businesses are expected to move much more sustainably and environmentally friendly. This study explores the key resources needed for adopting micro-culinary industry 4.0 in supporting sustainable business and circular economy macro-effects. The method used in this study is a systematic review of PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review). This research has determined the criteria for selected journal articles: scientific articles, publications and relevance to industry 4.0, micro and small sectors from 2019 to 2024. The result has 36 key resource industry 4.0 for culinary SMEs. The use of key resources can increase the circular productivity of culinary businesses in developing countries, especially by adapting digital and green economic forces.

articleTitle: The Role of Waqf in Islamic Life Insurance: The Dual Benefits of Insurance and Investment in View of Fatwa of Indonesian Ulema Council
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study explores the dual benefits of waqf in the context of Islamic life insurance, focusing on the advantages of waqf insurance and investment as stipulated by Fatwa DSN-MUI No. 106/2016. Employing a descriptive qualitative research approach, the study investigation draws from Islamic legal sources including al-Qur'an, al-Hadith, and fiqh rules to analyze waqf's role in Islamic life insurance. The study adopts a multidisciplinary perspective, incorporating usul al-fiqh, fiqh, hadith science, Islamic economics, and the philosophy of Islamic law. It recognizes the ijtihadi nature of waqf, encompassing various forms of ijtihad, and underscores ijtihad's pivotal role in achieving Sharia objectives. The findings emphasize the binding nature of the principles outlined in Fatwa DSN-MUI No.106 of 2016, obligating adherence by individuals seeking the fatwa, Islamic Financial Institutions, and clients. Waqf insurance offers enduring benefits, while waqf investment benefits are influenced by its temporary or perpetual nature. This study underscores the significance of waqf in Islamic finance, emphasizing compliance with the principles set forth in the fatwa for institutional and individual stakeholders.

articleTitle: Exploring Production Determinants in Aceh's Clothing SMEs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study examines the influence of capital, labor, raw materials, and technology on production in Aceh's small clothing industries across 23 districts/cities from 2018 to 2022. Based on the results of panel data testing using the Common Effect Model, this study found that labor, raw materials and technology have a significant effect on the production of small clothing industries in Aceh. While the capital variable has no effect on the production of small clothing industries in Aceh. Implications extend to policymakers, who should prioritize skill development, raw material access, and technological innovation. Industry practitioners can enhance labor, optimize materials, and integrate technology for competitiveness. Further research could explore capital's role and specific technology and labor impacts. These findings inform strategies for sustainable growth in Aceh's small clothing industry.

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Growth Management: Analyzing the Consequences of Ecological Deterioration in Asian Countries on Energy Consumption, Economic Growth and Financial Progress
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The paper examines complex relationship between energy consumption, economic growth, financial development, and environmental quality in 30 Asian countries from 2000 to 2022. The study utilizes panel data from a sample of Asian nations over the time period to investigate the dynamics and interdependencies among these variables. The research employs advanced econometric techniques such as the Pool Mean Group (PMG) estimator and panel unit root tests to analyze the data. The findings highlight the significant impact of energy consumption on environmental degradation and emphasize the need for sustainable energy solutions in the region. Economic growth and financial development are identified as influential factors in environmental deterioration, emphasizing the importance of balancing economic expansion with environmental sustainability. It also underscores the need for more effective environmental laws and regulations in the studied economies. The research provides valuable insights into the complex dynamics of energy, economy, finance, and the environment in Asian countries. The findings have suggestions for policymakers and stakeholders in promoting sustainable development and mitigating ecological deterioration in Asia.

articleTitle: Towards an Ethical Use of Big Data Analytic in Current Islamic Banking Corporate
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to identify and analyze how big data analytics technology affects ethic of Islamic banking. An organized previous studies and literature assessment were done via Scopus, Emerald, ScienceDirect, JSTOR, ProQuest, and Web-of-Science including a five-years timeframe (2016–2021). Around 38 previous studies recognized, 8 peer-reviewed previous studies of a significant journal were chosen. Regarding big data analytics, most big data analytics studies highlighted enhancing request completion, services process organization along with request movement operations. Though, a little research assessing an ethical concern of big data in banking & financial operations can recognized, saying such thing big data technology is recognized to enhance and give a worth in banking services operations. This an essential related to utilizing empowering machineries for realizing such possible initiative volume that big data can discovered. Results propose innovative study associated with Costing and commercialization operation, the banking and financial services operations, as well a costing and investment of big data in banking and financial industry, well designed approaches, modern digital patterns with modern corporate patterns. an assessment includes only academic researches of journals reflected a highly related (retrieved of detailed catalogues), utilizing a influence aspects like a valued standard. These results may assist banking and financial directors well recognized a possible for big data analytic, for example a key tools recognized via previous studies with literature and the influences on banking/financial processes and operations. The essential behind allowing machineries to control banking & financial performance are recognized along with a developing financial patterns or commercial patterns which big data arrangement can allow is emphasized. Research participates in satisfying such gap in a previous studies utilizing a organized previous studies with literatures assessment that in which way big data expertise influence banking and financial routine via contented investigation, via an financial outline for clarifying that banking and financial operations are influenced. Research papers of very essential journals since the period of 2016 to 2021 are recognized.

articleTitle: Executive Isolation of First-Generation Entrepreneurs in India: Are the company policies and culture to blame?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Entrepreneurship or developing one's own business venture is a very popular choice of new age professionals. This has also brought about a wave of first-generation entrepreneurs, who are individuals who start and aspire to establish their own businesses without any inherited family business or entrepreneurial experience. The first-generation entrepreneurs often have issues related to networks, resources and developing a sustainable culture and policies in their growing ventures. These first-generation entrepreneurs tend to rely on their determination, and vision to develop successful ventures from scratch. While the first-generation entrepreneurs are expected to play a vital role in job creation, and fostering innovation, they also have challenges of facing executive isolation due to their inexperience and intention to succeed fast. These entrepreneurs often get very busy with pursuing their entrepreneurial dreams and becoming role model, while undermining the impact of not developing a culture and policy framework that is sustainable. Thereby, executive isolation is a situation whereby such entrepreneurs tend to experience loneliness due to power distance and certain cost-effective policies, which in the long run would be detrimental to the psychological wellness of the entrepreneurs. The factor leading to executive isolation of first-generation entrepreneurs is not studied in detail and hence the outcomes of how can they be mitigated are also very limited. The current study intends to research about the impact of culture and policies on the executive isolation of the first-generation entrepreneurs and the body of knowledge will extend to further research opportunities on how to help these passionate venture founders mitigate the impacts of loneliness at the workplace.

articleTitle: Work-Family Conflict's Influence on Job Satisfaction. A Mediator Role of Emotional Exhaustion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The study object is to fulfil the earlier studies' gaps by observing the connection between and job satisfaction (JS) and work-family conflict (WFC). It aims to study the role of emotional exhaustion as a mediator between elements of job demands and job satisfaction. A sample of 269 respondents were customer service employees across 13 Palestinian banks. The analysis was done by the partial least squares path modelling method. The analysis showed that WFC positively affect emotional exhaustion. According to prospects, job demands have insignificant negative direct influence on job satisfaction. Also, emotional exhaustion decreases customer service employees' job satisfaction. And for the mediating relationship, there's a full mediation of emotional exhaustion among job satisfaction and job demands (WFC). Lastly, this article contributes to the literature using the JD-R model theory.

articleTitle: Towards Corporate Governance of University-Industry Partnerships in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: In accreting the importance of University-Industry Partnerships (UIPs) as one of the crucial types of research collaborations, Bahrain's Economic Vision 2030 clearly states “to encourage research collaborations to achieve sustainability and create a platform for a knowledge-based economy”. Following that, many empirical researches have studied the effectiveness of UIPs, yet, none of them tackled the factors needed to achieve a corporate governance of UIPs, especially in GCC. This quantitative research aims at testing empirically the impact of corporate governance factors on the effectiveness of UIPs in Bahrain. Delphi protocol was used to develop the preliminary conceptual framework, using a sample of 7 SMEs, which was then tested empirically using online survey through a sample of 79 respondents (including university-professors, and industry-experts). For testing research hypotheses, non-parametric tests were employed. Results revealed a positive relationship between 4 categories of corporate governance factors (i.e. University, Industry, Operational, and Relationship) and the effectiveness of UIPs in Bahrain.

articleTitle: Business Incubators' Sustainability in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This article addresses the UN Millennium Declaration, which seeks to reduce poverty and promote human dignity, equality, peace, democracy, and sustainability. Global development began with the Millennium Development Goals. The Millennium Development targets (MDGs) fulfilled these promises by identifying eight interrelated targets that the world could attain by 2015.The 2030 Agenda's global objectives link sustainability's three most fundamental elements-natural, social, and economic. Bahrain struggles to keep up with its fast-growing population due to its tiny area and limited resources. The Kingdom's GDP was BD 12,245 million (USD 32.5 billion) in 2017, impacted by Arab and Gulf turmoil since 2011. This uncertainty has affected the Kingdom's oil-and-gas-based economy, which has a 65% export-to-import ratio. The research finds that Bahrain must address population growth, urbanization, and land shortages. Population expansion, infrastructural development, and climate change threaten Bahrain's rich and varied maritime environments. These risks affect the economy, society, and environment greatly. Incubators speak about four success phases. Lower-range incubators don't consider environmental management. Second-category incubators sell environmental management heavily. According to their data, incubators that apply environmental management practices are in the third quartile and those with excellent standards are in the fourth.

Author Keywords: The Global Universities Partnership on Environment and Sustainability
the United Nations Educational Scientific and Cultural Organization

articleTitle: Is Al Salam Bank the Next Big Thing? Forecasting ASBB's Stock Prices Using FB-Prophet Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: One of the most prominent Islamic banks in the Kingdom, Al Salam Bank, has long been at the forefront of Fintech innovation in Bahrain. We have seen the organization experience substantial expansion in recent years in terms of its market share and brand image. In this study, we employed the prevalent FB-Prophet machine-learning model to predict ASBB's stock price in the future. We also consulted with four well-known Bahrain-based social media influencers to get their perspective on the potential impact of digital marketing on stock price growth. We concluded with favorable quantitative findings for ASBB's stock prices, which are expected to continue growing, after an in-depth analysis. Furthermore, our panel of influencers provided a substantial correlation between effective marketing strategies and resulting positive financial growth.

articleTitle: Investor Decision-Making Dynamics: Fundamental and Bandarmology Information on Aggressive Investor Behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to look at the effect of fundamental information and bandarmology information on aggressive investor behavior on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. This study uses a questionnaire as a data collection tool which is then processed and analyzed. The sample of this study was 981 investors spread throughout Indonesia. The data analysis used in this study used structural equation modeling using smartPLS. The results of this study indicate that fundamental information has no effect on aggressive investor behavior. While Bandarmology information has a positive and significant effect on aggressive investor behavior. This suggests that information about bookmaker activity in the stock market has a strong impact on how aggressive investors make their investment decisions. By having better access and understanding of the bookie's actions, aggressive investors tend to be more confident and tend to follow the bookie's actions in their reactions to market changes. For capital market regulators and supervisors, these findings suggest the need to closely monitor the use of Bandarmology information to prevent inefficient or manipulative market behavior.

articleTitle: Impact of Metaverse in Healthcare based on Architecture, Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The Metaverse represents a rapidly-evolving archetype of the next generation of digital worlds, that seeks to create a fully engaging, hyper-spatiotemporal, shared space for people to work and play. Recent advances in emerging technologies such as virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence, and blockchain are driving the metaverse from a hypothetical iteration to an upcoming reality. In the wake of the Covid-19 pandemic, healthcare systems worldwide have faced significant limitations, making it imperative to explore alternative healthcare solutions. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of how healthcare is evolving with the metaverse across six domains: telemedicine, clinical care, education, mental health, physical fitness, and pharmaceuticals. We examine the applications of the metaverse in these domains, discuss the technical issues involved, and propose solutions for developing future-proof medical systems using metaverse technology. The architecture is presented for implementing the metaverse in the healthcare sector and identifies key challenges that are currently impeding the global adoption of the metaverse in healthcare. Finally, we suggest open research directions for building healthcare systems using metaverse technology,

articleTitle: Indian Politics and Foreign Direct Investment: An Empirical Analysis Using ARDL Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The nation's policymakers have consistently recognized FDI as a crucial component of economic progress, and the country's political environment impacts the flow of FDI. Consequently, understanding the interplay between FDI inflow and the political climate is paramount for devising effective strategies that foster sustainable economic growth. It becomes essential to study the role of variables of the political environment (political stability and Control of corruption efforts) on the FDI inflow and in economic development and find out the degree of relation between variables of a political environment with the FDI inflow and con-integration among the variable using well know and proven time series technique of Auto Regressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) method. The result of the study indicates that both the variables (political stability and Control of corruption) do not work in the short run, but both are significant in the long run. Political stability positively impacts the FDI inflow if there is improvement in the country's political stability, while Control of corruption negatively impacts the FDI inflow.

articleTitle: The Role of Banks in Income Disparity Reduction in Indonesia: Islamic vs. Conventional Banks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Islamic and conventional banking in reducing income disparity in Indonesia. Based on the test using ARDL model, this study found two primary results. First, variables in Islamic banking such as total financing and third-party funds significantly reduce income disparity both in the long run and short run, while variables such as non-performing financing, and return on assets, contribute in the short run only.
