Second, variables in conventional banking such as total credit, non-performing loans, and third-party funds have a significant long-run impact on income disparity reduction, whereas all conventional banking variables significantly reduce income disparity in short run. The study's results have profound implications. Islamic banking institutions should strategically utilize their core principles to promote inclusion and effectively respond to the evolving requirements of society. Conventional banking institutions have the capacity to include socially responsible activities in order to achieve equitable outcomes. Finally, policymakers should foster a diverse financial sector, supporting Islamic banking growth and encouraging conventional banks to prioritize fairness. This approach aligns with Indonesia's socio-economic goals for a balanced financial landscape.

articleTitle: Digital Wallet Adoption in Supporting Financial Inclusion: A Conceptual Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The integration of fintech and banking has given rise to digital wallets, transforming global financial transactions and contributing to the advancement of financial inclusion. These wallets facilitate electronic payments and data access via devices, catering to the demand for secure and convenient transactions. While adoption is on the rise worldwide, Brunei's uptake has been slower due to novelty. Introduced in 2018, BruPay gained popularity among millennials and Gen Z for its user-friendly features. The pandemic accelerated digital wallet use, leading to the emergence of new players like DST Pay and Progresif Pay. This paper employs the UTAUT model to develop a framework elucidating the factors influencing local digital wallet adoption. It integrates constructs originating from literature, based on the clusters of personal belief (i.e., performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social belief), product attributes (i.e., customer support services, lifestyle compatibility, promotional benefits), and user's personality traits (i.e., personal innovativeness in information technology). The insights provide a contextual understanding of adoption trends in the country.

articleTitle: Green Finance : A Catalyst for Sustainable Future
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: In order to address the problems caused by climate change and environmental degradation, green finance has become an essential tool [1]. This study goes into the complex world of green finance, examining its theoretical foundations, important tools, legislative measures, and international trends. This study shows the importance of green finance in supporting sustainable development, encouraging environmental stewardship, and accelerating the shift to a low-carbon and resilient economy through a thorough analysis of the body of literature. The report also looks at opportunities and potential obstacles to further integrating green finance practices across diverse industries.

articleTitle: Improving Mosques' Performance Based on Financial Governance in Banda Aceh City, Indonesia: Does Religosity Play A Role?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The aim of this research was to explore how the introduction of asset management, debt management, and effective mosque governance impacted the performance of mosques in Banda Aceh City throughout 2021. Additionally, the study aimed to analyze how religiosity influenced mosque performance in the same city. Data was gathered via a questionnaire distributed to all 104 mosques in Banda Aceh City and analyzed using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The findings indicated that implementing asset management, debt management, and good mosque governance had a notable and positive impact on mosque performance. The level of religiosity also played a moderating role in the influence of asset management and good mosque governance on mosque performance. To enhance mosque performance, it is recommended that these results be utilized as a guide to enhance adherence to asset management and good mosque governance principles, as well as religiosity, to ensure effective and high-quality implementation. The study is anticipated to offer valuable insights for the Ministry of Religious Affairs in Banda Aceh, aiding them in enhancing mosque performance holistically and consequently contributing to the well-being of the mosques in the future.

articleTitle: Sustainability of Islamic Microfinance Institutions: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The current paradigms of Islamic economics and finance lead to comprehensive sustainability performance that considers Islamic Sharia goals. This paper presents a comprehensive literature review focusing on assessing the sustainability of Islamic Microfinance Institutions (IMFs) through various model measurements from a global perspective published in reputable international journals until 2023. The authors have applied several literature review techniques, including bibliometric citation and content analysis, to review past studies. The collected manuscripts comprise 52 papers published from 2008 to 2023, categorized into various research topics. The results indicate that research on sustainability performance in the Islamic finance sector is still scarce, despite experiencing a fairly fluctuating increase. The highest number of publications was in the year 2023, with a total of 11 papers (19<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) out of the overall publications. The findings from our research show that existing studies have used a variety of techniques to measure the sustainability of Islamic Microfinance Institutions (IMFs). The review highlights that the most frequently utilized models in measuring the sustainability of Islamic microfinance institutions use qualitative approaches. However, 37% of articles within the collection employ quantitative measurements. Previous research generally considers financial and social aspects or spiritual dimensions as separate elements.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Ownership Concentration (OC) on Dividends Using Return on Capital as a Moderator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This research paper targets to investigate the influence of ownership concentration (OC) on the dividend policy (DP) of 78 listed non-financial firms. Return on capital (ROC) is used to moderate the relationship between OC and DP. Data collected for analysis pertains to 2016–2020. The methodology adopted for analyzing data of these firms for the said period is the quantile regression panel data model (QRPDM). The models' findings show no significant impact of OC on the DP of these firms; however, under the influence of ROA, the relationship between OC and DP becomes significant. The limitation intrinsic to this study is the non-consideration of financial firms, which paves the way for further work in the area. This study is the first to take up OC, a crucial component of CG, and assess its impact on DP for India specifically.

articleTitle: Exploring the Nexus Between Digital Finance, Social Capital, Financial Literacy, and Islamic Financial Inclusion in Banda Aceh, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of Islamic financial literacy on Islamic financial inclusion through the mediation of digital finance and social capital. Proportionate Stratified Random Sampling was used to select 385 samples from each of Banda Aceh City's 9 sub-districts. Afterward, the questionnaire data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in accordance with scientific standards. This study found two important things. First, Islamic financial literacy, digital finance, and social capital boost Banda Aceh's Islamic financial inclusion. Second, digital finance and social capital can mediate the effects of Islamic financial literacy on Banda Aceh's Islamic financial inclusion. This study emphasizes the need for a holistic approach, combining education, technology, and community trust to promote Islamic financial inclusion. Policymakers, educators, institutions, and community leaders can leverage these insights to contribute to a more inclusive Islamic finance ecosystem.

articleTitle: The Use of Sharia Fintech Among Gen Z: Does Sharia Financial Literacy Play a Role?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The objective of this research is to explore and analyze the moderating role of sharia financial literacy in enhancing the relationship between perceived convenience, perceived benefits, and perceived security on the desire to use sharia financial technology (fintech) services among Gen Z in Banda Aceh City, Indonesia. From a total of 37,892 Gen Z individuals in the city, 150 respondents were selected as the research sample using a purposive sampling technique. The primary data were collected by distributing the questionnaires to the respondents and analyzed using the Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) method with the support of SEMPLS software. The study recorded that perceived convenience, perceived benefits, and perceived security have a positive impact on interest in using sharia fintech services. The study found an insignificant role of the sharia financial literacy in moderating the effects of perceived convenience, perceived benefits, and perceived security on interest in using sharia fintech services among Gen Z in Banda Aceh City. However, sharia financial literacy positively influenced interest of using sharia fintech services. Thus, to increase interest of Gen Z in using sharia fintech services, it is important to increase sharia financial literacy, perceived convenience, perceived benefits, and perceived security among Gen Z.

articleTitle: Board Characteristics And Financial Firms Performance In GCC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: The study aims to bring forth evidence of the link among various boards' characteristics with the financial performance of banks operating within GCC markets. The sample consists of 97 banks with the time-series-cross-section (TSCS) data spanning for 10 years from 2010 to 2019. Non-financial sector firms have been excluded, as every sector has a different set of regulations and operating activities. The Random Effects model is employed for analysis. Findings reveal that the board meetings, board independence, and female board members have a negative and significant effect on the financial performance, which is measured by ROA (Return on Assets). However, the board size was found to be insignificant in the GCC financial firm context.

articleTitle: A Rising Trend in the Non-Performing Assets in the Education Loan Category: A New Concern for Indian Banking Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: Education loans play a vital role in providing financial support to students, and surmounting Non-performing assets (NPAs) could affect credit growth, hindering access to quality education and impacting the economy's productivity. Understanding the relationship between macro factors and defaults will help predict future possibilities and mitigate risks in the education loan sector. Against this backdrop, this study investigates the relationship between the macro conditions of the country on the NPAs, in the context of India. While education loans are crucial for skill formation and enhancing productivity, the increasing NPAs are concerning, as they may lead to potential dropouts due to financial constraints. The study focuses on macro factors like gross enrollment ratio, the number of higher education institutions, and the unemployment rate to explain the defaults in educational loans. However, the study does not find a statistically significant impact of these macro factors on surging NPAs. It suggests future research should explore borrower-specific and loan category-specific factors, such as gender, course opted, interest rates, collateral, credit risk analysis, and loan duration. Banks can use the findings to reassess their lending strategies and risk assessment models for educational loans. Policymakers can utilize the results to design targeted interventions and policies to address NPAs and ensure access to education for meritorious students. Students may benefit from improved loan terms and increased availability of educational funding options.

articleTitle: Exploring the Alignment of Integrated Reporting with Value-Based Intermediation and its Adoption in Key Islamic Finance Nations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study investigates the alignment between Integrated Reporting (IR) and Value-Based Intermediation (VBI), along with the level of IR adoption among Islamic banks included in the top countries listed in the Islamic Finance Country Index (IFCI). Employing a qualitative descriptive approach, we conducted content analysis on integrated and annual reports from 28 Islamic banks operating in Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, and Malaysia between 2019 and 2021. This analysis involved a comparison of VBI components with IR content elements, drawing insights from relevant literature and documents. It is inferred that Islamic banks openly adopting IR also integrate it into their reporting practices. The findings reveal similarities between VBI components and IR content elements, with the majority of component VBI disclosures related to IR content elements. The overall focus of VBI is on the company's vision and mission, employees, community, governance, environment and products. IR focuses on an overview of the organization and external environment, company outlook, governance, and business model. In addition, this study shows that relatively few Islamic banks adopt IR in their reporting. These include Bank Islam Malaysia Berhad (BIMB), Bank Muamalat Malaysia Berhad (BMMB), Maybank Islamic Berhad, Malaysia Building Society Berhad (MBSB), AI-Rajhi Bank, and Saudi Investment Bank (SAIB).

articleTitle: Determining The Intention to Visit Foreign Tourists to Sabang, Aceh, Indonesia: Halal Awareness as Moderation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study examines the effect of halal image and attitude on the intention to visit foreign tourists in Sabang, Aceh. This study tested halal awareness as a moderator variable in the hypothesized relationship. This survey is a self-administered questionnaire that is disseminated online to selected international travellers around the world. Using a non-probability quota sampling technique, 100 samples were used for further data analysis. Data were analyzed using Smart PLS software. The findings of this study indicate that the halal image and attitude significantly influence the intention of foreign tourists to visit tourist destinations in Sabang, Aceh. The relationship between halal image and attitude towards the intention to visit foreign tourists is moderate by halal awareness. This study provides empirical evidence that halal image and attitude significantly affect foreign tourists' intention to visit destinations in Sabang, Aceh. As for the practical implications, the findings of this study must improve the halal image and attitude that can encourage tourists to visit tourist destinations in Sabang. It is hoped that tourist destinations can increase halal awareness following the expectations of tourists in the future.

articleTitle: Green Financing for Sustainable Economic Growth: Exploring Critical Factors Towards Resilient Economies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study investigates the role of green financing in promoting sustainable economic growth and explores the critical factors that contribute to building resilient economies. Green financing, which encompasses investments and financial practices that prioritize environmental sustainability, has gained increasing attention as a means to address pressing environmental challenges while fostering economic prosperity. Green finance development involves investments, loans, and financial products that prioritize environmental sustainability, resource conservation, and pollution reduction. The findings indicate that Green Credit and Green Securities have significant positive effects on economic growth in the long run, emphasizing the importance of integrating green financing practices into the financial system. The paper contributes to the growing body of literature on green finance and its role in shaping sustainable economic growth. Using data from the World Bank for the period 1995 to 2020, this research examines the relationship between green financial development indicators, namely Green Credit, Green Securities, Green Insurance, and Green Investment, and their impact on Economic Growth. Questionnaire survey is used to conduct quantitative analysis resulting in descriptive statistics, correlation matrix and augmented dickey-fuller test. By embracing green financing practices and understanding their impact on various economic sectors, policymakers, financial institutions, and businesses can work together to build resilient economies that safeguard the environment for future generations.

articleTitle: Does Halal Certification Policy Through Self-Declare Effective at Attracting More Halal-Certified MSEs? Evidence from Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance (SIBF)
abstract: This study aims to determine the extent to which the effectiveness of the halal assurance system through efforts to self-declare SME halal certification is relevant to the assistance of the halal production process (PPH) in East Java. This research was conducted from August 2022 to December 2022 using primary data obtained from interviews with experts consisting of BPJPH, halal assistants, and SMEs that have participated in halal certification. The data were analyzed with descriptive qualitative methods. The results of this study state that for the four indicators of program effectiveness, namely indicators of program target accuracy and program monitoring indicators, the categories are quite effective. Meanwhile, indicators of program socialization and indicators of program objectives are categorized as ineffective. This ineffectiveness is due to the non-achievement of the target of the halal certification program in 2022 which is due to the lack of optimal PPH assistants in carrying out assistance to business actors. This research can be used by policymakers to make improvements to make halal certification more effective according to the findings of this study. This research is the first research related to the halal certification program through self-declared after the implementation of halal certification through self-declared in 2022.
